items.excerpt:
It seems like every week yet another company is offering driverless forklifts. But how well are they actually selling? And will all those vendors survive?
The number of companies offering forklifts that can lift, lower, pick, put away, and transport loads without a human operator on board has exploded. At material handling shows in the U.S., Europe, and Asia, dozens of companies from around the world are exhibiting driverless (a.k.a. robotic or automated) lift trucks. They’re just the tip of the iceberg, though: One industry executive estimates that hundreds of companies offer automated forklifts today—some large and well-established, but many of them tiny and untested.
Although automated lift trucks have been available in the U.S. for more than a decade, only a limited number of fleets have adopted them, and it’s unclear how many units have been leased or sold to date. It’s also unclear whether the market for driverless forklifts can support so many vendors. To get some sense of the near-term outlook for this equipment—primarily automated trucks with masts and forks—we looked at the current market, what is driving or constraining adoption, and how much demand is expected to grow.
When it comes to suppliers of driverless forklifts, vendors fall into two main categories. The first includes original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) of manual lift trucks that have added automated forklifts to their lineups. In the U.S., that list includes such familiar names as Toyota, Raymond, Crown, Hyster, Yale, Linde, and Big Joe, among others.
The second category could be called “robotic from the start” and includes Seegrid, Rocrich AGV Solutions (a joint venture between Logisnext Americas Inc. and Jungheinrich that sells Rocla and Jungheinrich automated forklifts in North America), Oceaneering, Fox Robotics, VisionNav, and Vecna Robotics, to name just a few of the many players.
We spoke to companies in both categories for this article. Each one offers a different mix of products, including automated counterbalanced trucks, pallet stackers, reach trucks, very narrow aisle (VNA) equipment, and tow tractors, which are also known as tuggers. Some automated forklifts are versatile, while others are very specialized. Equipment offered by Fox Robotics, FlexNav, and Gideon, for example, is specifically designed for loading and unloading trailers and containers.

items.title: Meta 详解 Thin Orchestrator 模式：让路由少干活提升 AI 智能体可靠性
items.description: Meta 工程团队介绍其数据管道智能体采用的瘦编排器（thin orchestrator）模式：一个约 1300 行的编排器只负责路由和可靠性检查，将 20+ 工作流分派给 14 个上下文隔离的专项子智能体，自身不做任何领域推理。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/qh6pvehounuylklti7i0zl124
items.excerpt:
The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do
Meta 工程团队介绍其数据管道智能体采用的瘦编排器（thin orchestrator）模式：一个约 1300 行的编排器只负责路由和可靠性检查，将 20+ 工作流分派给 14 个上下文隔离的专项子智能体，自身不做任何领域推理。
Meta 工程团队给出可直接迁移的瘦编排器架构方法，用固定路由协议和隔离子智能体降低生产智能体的幻觉风险。
我们构建了一个 1,300 行的编排器，将 20 多个工作流路由到 14 个专业 AI 智能体。它本身不执行任何领域工作。这正是关键所在。
当我们首次部署 AI 智能体，在 Meta 的推荐系统中自动化数据列接入时——这一流程横跨三个代码仓库、三种编程语言，以及最多六个必须保持同步的管道阶段——我们做了大多数团队都会做的事：构建一个无所不知的智能体。
解决办法不是更好的提示词或更大的上下文窗口，而是让中央智能体承担更少的任务。我们称之为薄编排器模式：一个负责排序和可靠性检查的路由器，把所有领域决策都留给专业智能体。
我们的管道采用配置即代码的方式：Python 配置驱动 C++ 代码生成，C++ 代码生成再供给数据处理服务，数据处理服务再填充分析系统。接入单个数据列需要跨配置注册表、后端服务和数据管道进行协调变更，每个数据列在数据到达之前要经过最多六个阶段。
我们的第一种方法是使用一个单一的 AI 智能体，为它加载所有领域知识、配置模式、代码生成规则、管道路由逻辑、验证要求，以及 10 多个数据源的填充模式。
超过某个上下文阈值后，额外的知识会 降低 而非提升性能。智能体会交叉污染概念，把一个子系统的字段命名约定应用到另一个子系统，或者在从不同数据源填充时使用本应属于某个数据源的代码生成模式。西奈山 Windreich 人工智能与人类健康系的一篇 预印本 发现，在 80 个任务的批次中，编排式多智能体系统保持了 65.3% 的准确率，而单智能体则降至 16.6%，同时令牌使用量最多减少 65 倍。作者将此归因于该设计对任务的隔离，从而防止了上下文干扰。我们经历的恰恰相反：单个智能体淹没在自己的知识中。
我们还评估了另一种单智能体方案。在 为 每个任务手动进行提示词工程的情况下，其成功率为 70-80%：工程师必须为每个具体任务精心编写自定义系统提示词。没有这种人工辅助，成功率降至 10-20%。这不是提示词工程的问题，而是架构的问题。
第 1–5 步和第 7 步是确定性的。只有第 6 步涉及大语言模型（LLM）推理，而且它发生在仅加载了自身领域知识的隔离子代理内部。
一个架构洞见是将 需要发生什么 与 每一步如何执行 分离。编排器通过工作流模板定义阶段顺序——这些确定性状态机约束了 LLM 的决策空间：
每个工作流模板都以不同顺序复用同一组 14 个子代理。当我们需要支持管道迁移这一全新用例时，我们没有构建新代理。我们编写了一个新的工作流模板，以不同方式排列现有代理。零新增代理代码。完整的生产级能力。
这种统一性意味着添加新子代理是模板化工作，而非从零开始的工程。第 15 个子代理在结构上与第一个完全相同。
知识文件在子代理执行时按需加载，而不是嵌入到编排器中。我们按工作流领域维护了 25+ 个知识文件。当知识文件更新时，下一个会话会自动使用最新版本——无需更改编排器。相同的知识文件服务于我们代理的多个平台实现。
为新列准备配置，手工需要三到四天，用我们早期的配置驱动系统大约需要一天。瘦编排器系统在不到一小时内完成。
更广泛的背景：系统约三分之二的变更无需大量人工编辑即可落地。它通过用通用性换取深度领域知识来实现这一点，这是一种刻意的架构选择。编排器是通用的；子代理是专家。
传统方法是让编排器成为最聪明的组件——给它所有上下文，让它推理该做什么以及如何做。这在失效之前一直有效，而它恰好在最需要它的时候失效——在规模化、复杂多步工作流、跨异构子系统时。
支持薄编排器的最有力论据，是另一种方案的失败模式。当重量级编排器产生幻觉时，错误会向下游一切扩散：它会路由到错误的代理、收集错误的字段，或跳过可靠性检查。薄编排器几乎没有产生幻觉的空间，因为它的路由和可靠性步骤不依赖 LLM 推理。它遵循固定协议。创造力发生在下游，在隔离的、领域受限的上下文中，那里幻觉风险被最小化，失败也被限制在局部。
我们正在扩展这一架构，以应对新流水线领域中数据列的增加。组合式论点预测这会奏效，因为扩展意味着添加工作流模板和知识文件，而不是重建代理。我们还在探索系统如何从生产使用中持续改进，利用自动化反馈循环识别失败模式，并对子代理知识提出有针对性的改进建议，同时始终由人工审核把关任何变更。
反直觉的教训：我们 AI 代理系统中最重要的组件，是干活最少的那个。让编排器保持薄、让专家保持深，整个系统就会变得更可靠。
这项工作是一次团队努力。其他为此做出贡献的人包括： Mani Bhushan、Rahul Maliakkal、Jae Ha、Chakrapani Kumar、Vivek Tiwari 和 Amanda Yin。

In our continuing series of discussions with top supply-chain company executives, Lit Fung talks about expanding business overseas, the software behind AMRs, and future robotic innovations.
A specialist in artificial intelligence, robotics, and intelligent logistics, Lit Fung is managing director and vice president of international business and the Americas at warehouse robotics and automation company Geek+ . Among other accomplishments, he led Geek+’s first overseas deployments and has built its international organization and partner ecosystem in more than 40 countries, overseeing strategy, sales, delivery, and customer success across these international markets.
Q: HOW WOULD YOU DESCRIBE THE CURRENT MARKET FOR WAREHOUSE ROBOTICS?
A: The market has entered a new phase of maturity. When we first started, many companies we spoke with viewed warehouse robotics as an innovation project, which often led to proof-of-concept projects. Today, it’s increasingly considered a strategic business investment largely driven by persistent labor shortages, rising customer expectations, and SKU [stock-keeping unit] proliferation.
The need for greater supply chain resilience has fundamentally changed how companies think about warehouse operations. As a result, automation is no longer just about reducing labor costs; companies also want to create more agile, scalable, and predictable operations.
Q: YOU WERE INSTRUMENTAL IN ESTABLISHING GEEK+ AS AN INTERNATIONAL PLAYER. ARE THERE SOME LESSONS YOU LEARNED IN LAUNCHING OPERATIONS IN MULTIPLE COUNTRIES?
A: One of the biggest lessons is that while logistics challenges are remarkably similar around the world, every market is different with respect to how business gets done. Success requires much more than shipping technology into a new country. It requires local talent, trusted partners, responsive service, and a willingness to understand each customer’s operating environment.
Q: WHERE DOES SOFTWARE FIT INTO A SUCCESSFUL ROBOT INSTALLATION?
A: Robots execute physical tasks, but software orchestrates the entire operation. Without intelligent software, even the most advanced robots cannot operate at their full potential. The software determines task prioritization, traffic management, inventory movement, resource allocation, and integration with warehouse management systems and enterprise platforms.

Numan 一手复盘 AI 健康教练的评测体系建设，给出的固定数据集、模拟对话和临床医生签核准则等做法可迁移到其他受监管场景。
Numan 是一家英国数字健康公司，帮助患者在体重、激素和性健康方面管理长期病症。我们的许多患者正在参与减重项目，并每天使用该应用来跟踪进展。
在构建 Nu（我们的 AI 健康教练）时，我们的设计挑战之一是在不越过医疗诊断、处方或做出临床决策这条红线的前提下，提供高质量的健康指导——在我们这个高度监管的医疗领域，这些都是智能体的严格边界。虽然我们最初关注的是智能体及其周围的自动化，但最终最重要的却是我们评估标准的质量。这就是我们如何开发并改进评估标准，以提供高质量用户体验、同时避开受监管领域的故事。
我们从大多数团队起步的地方开始：一个包含输入和预期输出的数据集，以及一个对每条回复打分的 LLM 评判器。这套方法对问答型智能体很有效，但教练式指导是一场对话，而不是一个答案。所有预先固定 Nu 回复的方法都在两个方面失败了：
1. 基于静态固定样本的单轮评估 （固定输入、固定预期输出，评判器单独对一条回复打分）。行为式教练指导很少对某个提示只有一个正确答案，而一条回复是否安全取决于它周围的对话。Nu 需要在给出建议之前，理解在整个对话中是什么在阻碍患者，并在患者施压时守住正确的边界。
在整个数据集上平均一个分数，掩盖了 Nu 失败的地方。少数几条糟糕的回复几乎不会让数字变化，于是对话看起来合规，实际却并非如此。固定样本还导致了第二个问题。在一次运行中，一组低分结果被证明是评估本身的错，而不是 Nu 的错。评分标准期望在仅两轮的交流中同时体现共情、探索 和 建议，而人类教练会把这些分散在一场对话中。Nu 的指导是正确的，但狭窄、固定的评估错误地标记了失败。
2. 脚本化的多轮对话。 对单轮固定样本的明显修复方法，是预先写出患者预期的一系列回复。有了这个“脚本”，一个场景的若干轮对话被逐条喂给 Nu，评判器便可在最后对整个对话记录打分。虽然这比单条回复给了评判器更多空间，但评估还是以同样的方式崩溃了。当患者的第二轮回复是预先写好的，测试就忽略了 Nu 在第一轮实际说了什么。一旦 Nu 说了脚本没有预料到的话，之后的每一轮都在回复一场从未发生过的对话。
Nu 是一个 LangGraph 图。一个监督模型负责编排向领域专家子智能体的交接，每个子智能体专注于一个教练领域，拥有自己的提示词和工具。这种组合模型让新增专家变得成本低廉，更重要的是，它让所有专家的评估面保持统一。
Nu 需要做对的一些事情 确实 可以从单条回复中判定。例如，主管是否路由到了正确的专家、用药问题是否得到了安全的回答，或者安全防护是否拦截了它应当拦截的内容。针对这些，我们运行了主题数据集，覆盖辅导质量、安全性、用药查询、路由和摘要。与最初的单轮评估不同，我们改变了两点：1）每个数据集都由 LLM 评判器按类别评分，而不是取一个平均值，因此某一类别中的集中失败即使在其他类别看起来正常时也依然可见。2）每个评分标准只询问单条回复能够展示的内容，因此评判器不再因为 Nu 像教练那样把控对话节奏而惩罚它。
任何 fixture 无法覆盖的内容（即需要整段对话形态的内容）都有自己的一层，如下所述。由于 Nu 是一个图，评估可以针对整个系统或单个子代理，而新的专家会继承评估面。
构建评估的简单方式是使用一个单独的测试框架，复制代理的提示词并直接调用模型……这在测试框架与生产环境出现偏差之前是可行的。我们没有单独的测试框架，并遵循 我们交付的东西就是我们测试的东西 这一原则。每次评估都经过患者与之对话的同一个 LangGraph 图，因此我们评分的正是患者所遇到的。
随着规模扩大，我们开始质疑一个提供商是否适合所有代理，因为主管和领域专家从事不同的认知工作。Nu 目前运行在两个前沿提供商上，按代理选择：一个用于主管，另一个用于专家。得益于我们以开放、主题数据集形式构建的评估套件的可移植性——它可以指向任何配置——我们在不同提供商上运行了相同的数据集并并排阅读结果。前沿提供商之间的迁移通常需要数周的手动测试，而这次只花了一天。
根据 MHRA 的指导，具有医疗目的（提供临床建议、诊断或推荐治疗）的软件产品会成为医疗器械。Nu 被设计为用于生活方式辅导和教育的健康产品，而非临床护理。
让 Nu 保持在这一范围内是我们在每次变更时都会检查的事情。安全探针作为按类别指标运行并控制发布：那里的回归会阻止变更自动发布。我们朝着 安全完成 的方向调优，这是一种既守住底线又仍然听起来像教练的引导，因此提出超出范围问题的患者会得到温暖、有用的回答，而不是生硬的拒绝。
除了测试之外，防护节点在图中对每段对话运行。安全防护会在患者看到之前，依据一组固定的临床安全规则审查每条发出的回复。不安全的草稿会被送回主管重新生成。如果持续失败，消息会被替换为安全的回退内容，而不是交付不安全的回复。而且由于防护位于图中，它们也位于同一个评估面内——我们的一个主题数据集专门用于测试安全防护是否拦截了它应当拦截的内容。此外，健康教练每天审查真实对话的样本，并标记任何看起来像安全疏漏的内容，因此人类主题专家会校准什么算作安全。

items.description: Tesla’s latest Roadster demonstration was certainly impressive. It was an […] The post Tesla’s Flying Roadster Is Impressive. But What Does It Really Mean for Logistics? appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Tesla’s latest Roadster demonstration was certainly impressive. On October 15, at a SpaceX facility in Texas, the company demonstrated a redesigned sports car capable of accelerating from zero to 60 mph in under a second, maneuvering briefly in the air using compressed-gas thrusters, and driving upside down with a specialized suction system. It was an extraordinary engineering demonstration, but does it mean we’re getting closer to flying delivery vehicles?
Perhaps, although not necessarily in the way Tesla’s demonstration might suggest. For logistics executives, the more interesting development isn’t the prospect of flying cars. It’s the continuing convergence of aerospace technology, autonomous systems, and transportation software—and what that convergence could eventually mean for freight movement.
Tesla’s Roadster isn’t designed to carry freight. The company is targeting production in 2028, and the prototype hasn’t demonstrated sustained transportation flight, commercial payload capability, or the operating economics necessary for logistics applications. But the broader technology category is worth watching. Advanced air mobility encompasses emerging aircraft technologies that could support passenger transportation and specialized freight operations. The Federal Aviation Administration specifically identifies cargo movements between airports, cargo facilities, and distribution centers as potential applications.
The distinction matters. A sports car that briefly leaves the ground is fundamentally different from an aircraft designed to move freight reliably, repeatedly, and economically. While Tesla is demonstrating what’s technically possible, other companies are already putting autonomous aerial delivery into commercial operation.
Consider Walmart’s drone-delivery program. In May 2026, Walmart announced that it had completed more than one million drone deliveries, working with providers including Wing and Zipline. The company reported operations across 66 stores in four states, serving five metropolitan markets, with an average delivery time of 23 minutes. That’s an operating logistics service rather than a laboratory experiment, although one with important limitations.

Disney found a way to buy Character.AI without buying its lawsuits

在众多诉讼中代表原告的科技正义法律项目（Tech Justice Law Project）和社交媒体受害者法律中心（Social Media Victims Law Center）拒绝置评。
据现任首席执行官的声明，尽管在谷歌交易后失去了关键员工，并且据现任首席执行官称“始终”在盈利方面挣扎，Character.AI 仍继续开发 AI 工具，包括“与虚构角色进行实时音频驱动的 FaceTime 风格视频生成”。
2025 年 8 月，Character.AI 与一位投资银行家合作，试图寻找战略买家或投资者。根据破产申请文件，Character.AI 和该银行家收到“一致的反馈”，称其产品和用户群“令人印象深刻”，但周围的诉讼和“监管悬顶”使其无法被收购。
那年 11 月，Character.AI 得知一个由州总检察长组成的联盟已开始调查该公司。当该公司申请破产时，参与多州调查的州和地区数量已攀升至 46 个。

文件称，Character.AI 当时正在与各州就如何解决他们发现的问题进行谈判，但在宣布破产前未达成任何协议。
如果交易完成并获得法院批准，迪士尼将获得 Character.AI 的员工及其大部分技术栈，但将能够避开导致 Character.AI 垮台的持续法律问题，包括多州调查。
在破产中提交利益通知的各州已 明确表示 ，他们保留对任何破产计划提出质疑的权利，这可能会引发围绕破产最终结果的争斗。

items.title: Open Logistics API Takes Aim at Dock Scheduling
items.description: An open dock scheduling API promises fewer manual handoffs among carriers, shippers and warehouses. Pilot partners are being recruited for early 2027. The post Open Logistics API Takes Aim at Dock Scheduling appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Consider a familiar hypothetical dock scenario: the truck has arrived, the freight is ready, and the dock is available. Yet the driver is still waiting. Anyone who has spent time examining distribution operations knows how often the problem is not physical capacity but coordination. The carrier, warehouse, shipper, and appointment platform each have part of the information. Getting those systems to agree is another matter.
That familiar disconnect is the target of a new initiative from the Open Logistics Foundation. The organization has developed an open, vendor-neutral application programming interface (API) for time-slot management and is recruiting partners to test it in live operations. Transporeon and TradeLink have already implemented the interface, while broader pilot work is planned for early 2027.
The announcement is not a breakthrough in the ability to book a dock appointment. Software has done that for years. Its importance lies in an attempt to make appointments and relevant transport information portable across systems and companies without building a separate custom interface for every relationship.
A transportation management system may know a truck's planned arrival. A carrier may have an updated ETA. A yard system knows which trailers have checked in. A warehouse management system understands receiving workloads and labor availability. A dock appointment platform controls reservations. None of that guarantees the data will move accurately and promptly between them.
As a result, facilities still rely on emails, phone calls, portals, and manual rescheduling. An early truck can arrive before the facility is prepared; a delayed truck can hold a slot that another load could use. A booked appointment is not the same thing as an executable appointment.
The economics are straightforward. Waiting consumes driver time, equipment capacity, and receiving resources. It can generate detention charges while making dock labor harder to schedule. It also creates a feedback loop: unreliable appointments encourage facilities to build in slack, reducing effective capacity.
The technology industry has often approached these problems from the viewpoint of a particular application. But dock coordination crosses enterprise boundaries. No single TMS, WMS, or yard management supplier owns the full process.

items.title: Carbon Is Becoming a Constraint in Transportation Planning, Not Just a Reporting Metric
items.description: Transportation carbon is moving upstream from disclosure into planning. Once emissions can be estimated with sufficient consistency, carbon becomes another constraint to evaluate alongside cost, service, capacity, and risk. The post Carbon Is Becoming a Constraint in Transportation Planning, Not Just a Reporting Metric appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Executive thesis. Transportation carbon is moving upstream from disclosure into planning. Once emissions can be estimated with sufficient consistency, carbon becomes another constraint to evaluate alongside cost, service, capacity, and risk.
Historically, transportation emissions were often calculated after execution for reporting purposes. That is changing as organizations gain better shipment-level data and as sustainability objectives become more closely connected to operating decisions. Carbon can be considered before the load moves, alongside cost, service, capacity, and risk.
Mode, distance, equipment, utilization, empty miles, consolidation, routing, fuel, energy source, and carrier performance all influence transportation emissions. Those are also variables that transportation teams already manage for economic and service reasons. The opportunity is to incorporate emissions into the same decision environment rather than treat carbon as a separate reporting workflow.
Comparing alternatives requires consistent methods and defensible activity data. Carrier-provided values, standard factors, modeled estimates, and primary fuel or energy data may all have roles, but the system should preserve the method and confidence behind the result. Otherwise the organization risks optimizing against numbers that are not comparable.
The lowest-emissions option may not always satisfy service, cost, capacity, or operational constraints. That is precisely why carbon belongs inside the planning decision. Leaders need to see the tradeoff explicitly and decide where emissions should act as a target, a constraint, or one weighted objective among several.
The strongest transportation-emissions programs connect measurement to action: improve trailer or container utilization, reduce empty miles, change mode where feasible, select lower-emission equipment or fuels, redesign routes, adjust delivery frequency, or work with carriers on specific lanes. Measurement becomes valuable when it changes the transportation plan.
The Logistics Viewpoints Transportation Emissions Management: Technology, Data, and Measurement guide connects shipment-level carbon measurement to TMS planning, mode, utilization, empty miles, fuels, EVs, carrier data, and operational reduction levers.
The objective is not measurement for its own sake; it is to expose operational tradeoffs early enough for mode, routing, utilization, equipment, and carrier choices to change the outcome.

items.excerpt:
Typical safeguards around robotic palletizers consist of fixed sensors, but beRobox is taking a new approach by having safety detection move with the robot. The company today introduced the 3D Dynamic Safety module for its PALTZ palletizing systems.
“Safety has always been fundamental to automation, but we saw an opportunity to rethink how it could work on a palletizer,” stated David Demers, CEO of beRobox. “Our goal was not simply to introduce a new type of sensor. We wanted to create a safety concept that better reflects what is actually happening on the production floor: People interact with the system, pallets need to be changed, and the robot is constantly moving.”
Founded in 2022, beRobox said it has designed the PALTZ family of configurable palletizers for real-world production needs. The Sherbrooke, Quebec-based company claimed that its proprietary STACKiT software enables “true plug-and-play automation.” beRobox, whose global distribution network is growing, added that its mission is to solve challenges with smarter, simpler technology.
beRobox’s new safety module uses Sonair’s safety-certified ADAR One 3D ultrasonic sensor and integrates detection directly onto the robot arm. As the palletizer moves through its workspace, the sensor moves with it, creating a dynamic protective zone that continuously adapts to the robot’s position, said the company.
By knowing where the robot is and detecting people and objects around it in three dimensions, beRobox said its module can respond to what is happening within the palletizing workspace in real time. The result is a safety system that can be more selective in how it reacts to operator interactions, it asserted.

items.title: 黑客用 AI 智能体入侵 John Deere、SharkNinja 等超 100 家网站
items.description: AI 安全公司 Norforge 发现一名黑客用开源 AI 平台 Cairn 编排的智能体入侵了超过 100 个网站，据 Reuters 报道受害者包括 John Deere、SharkNinja 和 Cummins。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/tdcasw4dwhyzne3hxo3dmizmz
items.excerpt:
A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
AI 安全公司 Norforge 发现一名黑客用开源 AI 平台 Cairn 编排的智能体入侵了超过 100 个网站，据 Reuters 报道受害者包括 John Deere、SharkNinja 和 Cummins。
原文梳理了 Norforge 发现的暴露 Cairn 实例和受害企业回应，读者可以了解 AI 智能体大规模攻击的实际形态。
根据 AI 安全公司 Norforge 的 调查结果 ，一名黑客利用一支主要由 AI 代理组成的“大军”入侵了 100 多个网站，这些代理大多自主运作。虽然 Norforge 没有点名攻击目标，但 路透社 报道 称，受害者包括 John Deere、SharkNinja 和 Cummins 等公司。
随着技术日益先进， 人们对 AI 驱动的网络安全入侵的担忧 不断加剧，黑客利用这些工具发动大规模攻击。与此同时， 失控的 AI 代理在逃离测试环境后 也在自行发动攻击。
Norforge 的研究人员通过 Cairn 上暴露的工作内容发现了这些攻击。Cairn 是一个开源 AI 平台， 自称 为“通用问题求解引擎”。借助 Cairn，用户可以为 AI 代理设定起点和终点，代理在推进任务时会记录其进展。然而，正如 Norforge 所指出的，黑客也可以利用该工具，通过 AI 代理来策划网络攻击。
据 路透社 报道，入侵 100 多个网站的黑客是 Norforge 发现的暴露 Cairn 实例中“最活跃”的一个，他对位于美国、加拿大、澳大利亚和日本的公司发动了攻击。据 路透社 报道，这名攻击者用不到 100 个汉字列出了“首选入侵策略”，成功入侵耗时约 23 小时。总体而言，Nordforge 发现了 20 多个“可能具有恶意”的暴露 Cairn 实例。
在给 路透社 的一份声明中，John Deere 的一位发言人表示，“没有迹象表明敏感信息被访问”，此次攻击并未造成此类后果；而 Cummins 表示，它正在“调查有关我们一家第三方供应商运营的网站可能遭到网络攻击的报告”。
与此同时，SharkNinja 表示，此次入侵影响了一个包含产品支持信息的独立网站，并且它已控制住威胁。John Deere、Cumms 和 SharkNinja 没有立即回应 The Verge 的置评请求。
Nordforge 表示，它正在努力让恶意的 Cairn 实例下线。Cairn 的创建者（网名 @le1xia0） 本月早些时候表示 ，该平台“从来都不是‘黑客工具’”，并补充说“滥用是人的决定，而不是引擎的功能”。

items.description: Meta 介绍其位于俄亥俄州 New Albany 的吉瓦级超集群 Prometheus，一期已建成并用于训练 Muse 系列基础模型，目标扩展到约 100 万张 GPU。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ebl13m9gich6kfjixzvfiw5bq
items.excerpt:
Inside Prometheus: Meta’s Journey to a Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster
Meta 介绍其位于俄亥俄州 New Albany 的吉瓦级超集群 Prometheus，一期已建成并用于训练 Muse 系列基础模型，目标扩展到约 100 万张 GPU。
Meta 官方拆解其俄亥俄超集群的网络、散热与可靠性工程，读者可了解吉瓦级训练集群的实际运行细节。
目前，在俄亥俄州新奥尔巴尼，Meta 正在开展其迄今为止最具雄心的 AI 基础设施项目。Prometheus， 我们的吉瓦级超级集群， 是我们基础设施的一次进步，它正在训练下一代基础模型，这些模型将为数十亿人带来全新的 AI 体验。
两年前，新奥尔巴尼还是一个承载网络流量的常规数据中心站点。借助硬件、网络和建筑设计方面的进步，我们改造了这个站点，使其成为前沿模型训练项目的所在地。我们正在分阶段建设这座超级集群。第一阶段已经完成，并用于训练我们的 Muse 基础模型 ，包括 Muse Wonder 模型——这是我们新的前沿模型，在个人和专业智能体任务上实现了最先进的性能。
大规模训练任务需要一切以最优状态运行才能维持其性能；单台主机上的问题就可能拖慢或中止整个任务，降低其“有效算力利用率”（goodput）。通过专注于提升系统的稳定性和可靠性，我们在 Muse Wonder 的预训练运行中实现了超过 85% 的 goodput，在强化学习（RL）运行中实现了超过 90% 的 goodput。在这些训练运行期间，我们实现了约 47k GPU 小时的整体挂钟平均无中断时间（MTBI）。此后，我们在整个集群上实施了更多变更，包括固件修复，将 MTBI 提升至超过 54K GPU 小时，并且我们还在持续改进。
现在，我们正着眼于 Meta Superintelligence Labs 的下一代前沿模型，继续扩展 Prometheus。
https://engineering.fb.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/AIM-1210-Superclusters_Video_v1.mp4
如今，Prometheus 由分布在多栋互连建筑中的数十万块 GPU 组成，这些建筑包括传统数据中心建筑、AI 优化数据中心建筑以及快速部署结构，全部通过数英里的光纤紧密互连，作为一台单一机器运行。
这一容量使我们能够追求此前不切实际的更大模型和更长上下文窗口。在满规模状态下，Prometheus 将包含约 100 万块分布式 GPU，全部同步运行。
Prometheus 目前部署了两个 NVIDIA GPU 平台，第三个平台（基于 NVIDIA 的 Vera Rubin NVL72 ）即将到来。每个平台都代表着性能和效率的代际飞跃，依托我们的 NVL72 机架架构，其中 72 块 GPU 在同一网络结构内作为单个加速器运行。
我们的首个平台 Catalina 采用 NVIDIA GB200 NVL72。我们部署的是 Ariel 变体，这是一种双机架配置，每个机架中的 36 块 GPU 通过 NVLink 互连，构成一个统一的 72-GPU 域。与 Grand Teton H100 相比，Catalina 在原始算力和内存容量方面均有提升。它采用我们的 Open Rack V3 (ORv3) 高功率机架（HPR）结构，这是一种贡献给 Open Compute Project (OCP) 的开放硬件设计。
GB200 NVL72 的 Ariel 变体为每块 NVIDIA Blackwell GPU 搭配一颗 NVIDIA Grace CPU 和 2 块 NVIDIA ConnectX-7 400G 网卡，CPU 与 GPU 的比例为 1:1，使我们能够比业界其他厂商更早地为每块 GPU 部署 800G 的 I/O。我们选择 Ariel，是因为相对于 NVIDIA H100，GB200 NVL72 在几乎所有其他维度上都实现了扩展：FLOPS、HBM 带宽、scale-up 带宽和 scale-up 域规模，而每块 GPU 的 scale-out 带宽原本会停留在 400G。我们预计这种不均衡会损害性能，因此选择了为每块 GPU 提供 800G scale-out 的配置。这也让我们在区域扩展、800G scale-out 变得可用时，拥有更统一的规格。
https://engineering.fb.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/AIM-1210-Superclusters_GB200_GIF_v1.mp4
我们的第二个平台 Clemente 转向 NVIDIA GB300 NVL72，在 GPU 和平台层面均对 Catalina 有所改进。GB300 将每块 GPU 的 HBM 容量提升 1.5 倍，从 192 GB 增至 288 GB，密集 FP4 吞吐量也提升约相同倍数，同时注意力（softmax）加速大约翻倍。在平台层面，scale-out 不再是 GB200 NVL72 上的制约因素：NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNIC 原生提供每块 GPU 800G，因此我们早期在 Ariel 上部署的能力成为基线。再加上 2:1 的 GPU 与 CPU 比例，Clemente 能够将完整的 72-GPU 域装入单个机架，简化了我们的物理部署。Clemente 可采用我们的模块化风助液冷（AALC）部署，也可在我们新设计的数据中心中使用设施液冷（FLC）。由于线缆减少，可维护性也大幅提升。
https://engineering.fb.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/AIM-1210-Superclusters_GB300_GIF_v1.mp4
在传统 Web 服务中，数据中心网络在实例通常不需要高带宽、高性能以及跨多台服务器紧密锁步协调的

items.description: Robotic process automation gets sold to mid-size companies as the quick win. items.excerpt:
Robotic process automation gets sold to mid-size companies as the quick win. A bot logs into the same screens your staff use and clicks through them the way a person would, only faster. For a stable, rules-based task inside a system nobody can change, that works fine.
The trouble starts when a process runs across several tools that keep changing, or needs a bit of judgment along the way. At that point custom process automation, built on APIs and your own data instead of the user interface, usually costs less over a year than keeping the bots alive.
I’m CTO at udata , a software development company with 50+ engineers that builds automation systems and internal tools for growing businesses. Below is how we decide which approach fits, and what a custom build actually involves.
It would be unfair to write RPA off. Bots are a good answer when the target system is an old desktop application with no API and no vendor willing to add one. They also make sense for short-lived needs, like a migration that runs for two months and then disappears, or for a pilot where you want to prove that a process is worth automating at all before spending on a proper build.
Companies with strict change control like them for another reason. A bot doesn’t modify the underlying system, so it can get approved faster than an integration that writes to a production database.
If your situation looks like that, use the bot.
The typical problems show up later, once the bot has moved from pilot to something people depend on:
Usually the bot did its job. The process just grew past what screen-clicking can handle.
A custom build skips the screens. It talks to your systems directly through their APIs, runs scheduled sync jobs, and keeps its own database so every record has a history. Exceptions don’t vanish into a bot log. They show up in a small internal tool or dashboard where a person can fix them in a few clicks, and the fix feeds back into the rules.
Our usual stack for this is plain on purpose: Python with FastAPI or Node.js on the backend, PostgreSQL for storage, Docker for deployment. Nothing exotic, which matters when the client’s own team has to live with it later.
Where input is messy, we add a language model. Pulling fields out of an invoice or classifying an inbound email is exactly the kind of task that used to require a person and now doesn’t. items.title: AWS 发布 TorchNeuron：Trainium 的原生 PyTorch 后端
items.description: AWS 宣布 TorchNeuron，一个面向 Trainium 的开源原生 PyTorch 后端，10 月 20 日起以 Apache 2.0 公开 Beta 发布于 github.com/aws-neuron/torch-neuronx。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/szf3v3re4888fzekwoohhu8b4
items.excerpt:
Introducing TorchNeuron: Native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium
AWS 宣布 TorchNeuron，一个面向 Trainium 的开源原生 PyTorch 后端，10 月 20 日起以 Apache 2.0 公开 Beta 发布于 github.com/aws-neuron/torch-neuronx。
原文给出了 TorchNeuron 的执行模式、分布式支持与实测覆盖情况，读者可以据此评估现有 PyTorch 工作流迁移到 Trainium 的成本。
前沿模型涵盖语言、视频和音频，架构从稠密和混合专家 Transformer 到扩散、状态空间、世界和结构预测模型。PyTorch 是 AI 研究发生的地方，是定义模型的地方，也日益成为生产运行的地方。研究人员希望进行实验和创新，客户则希望获得 AWS Trainium 提供的性能，以实现其性能和规模目标。训练和推理库是针对 PyTorch 自身的 API 编写的，新的库和新版本持续发布。过去几年中，PyTorch 使这些 API 与加速器无关，并提供了用于注册自定义硬件的官方扩展点。
今天，为满足开发者和研究社区对 Trainium 日益增长的需求，我们很高兴在 10 月 20 日于北美 PyTorch Conference 开源发布之前，分享一种更简单的方法，将芯片作为标准 PyTorch 设备进行编程。AWS Trainium 是一系列 AI 芯片，专为下一代云规模 AI 训练和推理从头设计。我们宣布推出 TorchNeuron ，这是一个面向 Trainium 的开源原生 PyTorch 后端，使模型代码、库以及你已在使用的工具都能在 Trainium 上运行。这一集成直接建立在 PyTorch 社区创建的加速器无关扩展点之上，包括 PrivateUse1 设备后端和 torch.accelerator API。
TorchNeuron 在 Trainium2 和 Trainium3 上支持用于研究和调试的 eager 执行（包括性能改进的全新自适应 eager 模式）、用于生产性能的 torch.compile，以及用于自定义内核的 Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) 。此外，借助 Neuron Explorer ，性能工程师可以使用相同的 torch.profiler 追踪从框架到硬件的执行过程，将每个事件链接回其源代码行，从而精确定位瓶颈并高效优化。TorchNeuron 将以 Apache 2.0 许可证在 github.com/aws-neuron/torch-neuronx 开源发布，并于 10 月 20 日作为公开 Beta 版上线。
“PyTorch 的愿景很明确：开发者应在不同硬件平台上获得一致的体验。对 AWS Trainium 的原生支持扩展了这一选择，使研究人员和工程师能够使用他们已熟悉的 eager 执行和分布式 API 进行实验和迭代。团队可以利用 Trainium 的能力，而无需重新构建工作流或离开 PyTorch 生态系统。”——Meta PyTorch 工程总监 Jana van Greunen
快速开始非常简单。使用指针在 Trainium 上运行你的代码： .to('neuron') 。
针对 PyTorch 推荐的设备无关 API torch.accelerator 编写的现代代码无需修改即可运行。编译模型需要指定一次 Neuron 后端，使用 torch.compiler.set_default_backend("neuron") ，之后由 torch.compile(model) 接管，或按调用使用 torch.compile(model, backend="neuron") 。
TorchNeuron 通过 PrivateUse1（PyTorch 用于自定义硬件的官方扩展点）注册 Trainium，因此标准 API 可按原样工作： torch.nn 、 torch.tensor 、 torch.autocast 、 torch.distributed 和 torch.profiler 均在 neuron 设备上运行。PyTorch 的两种执行模式 eager 和 torch.compile 均可原生工作。
Eager 模式会立即执行操作，因此 Python 控制流、打印和断点都能正常工作，无需编译或跟踪步骤。这是用于研究和调试的模式。Eager 模式会逐个分派操作。每个操作直接执行时都会编译自己的 Neuron 可执行文件格式（NEFF）文件，在设备上启动它，并通过 HBM 移动其中间结果。我们还引入了自适应 eager 模式（实验性），以降低启动开销，并提供更好的操作融合机会，在不修改代码的情况下接近编译图的性能，同时保留交互式体验。
torch.compile(model, backend="neuron") 将模型捕获为图，由 Neuron 编译器进行优化，是用于稳定、高性能模型投入生产的模式。torch.compile 可用于优化整个模型或部分模型，并与 eager 模式无缝协作。原生支持 FlexAttention。TorchDynamo 将模型捕获为 FX 图，AOTAutograd 提前跟踪反向图，Neuron 后端通过 Torch-MLIR 将结果降为 StableHLO，Neuron 编译器生成在硬件上执行的 NEFF 文件。
Neuron 推理栈基于 TorchNeuron 中相同的 torch.compile 支持构建。vLLM Neuron 是 vLLM 的插件，用于服务 LLM；vLLM Omni Neuron 是 vLLM Omni 的插件，用于服务图像和视频生成的扩散模型。
广泛覆盖 aten 算子，涵盖文本、多模态与视觉语言、图像与视频生成和理解、状态空间模型以及世界模型中出现的算子

The University of Bradford is leading a £3.67 million Yorkshire Robotics Adoption Hub after securing £2.75 million in funding from Innovate UK to help manufacturers adopt robotics and automation technologies.
The Hub is designed to address one of the biggest barriers to productivity in UK industry.
The 42-month programme has secured £2.75 million in grant funding and brings together the University of Bradford, West Yorkshire Manufacturing Services (WYMS), the University of Huddersfield and Olympus Technologies, alongside a wider network of manufacturers, technology partners and regional stakeholders.
The Hub has been created in response to a growing adoption gap within UK manufacturing. While 73% of manufacturing SMEs say they intend to invest in automation, relatively few progress to implementation. The UK currently operates around 104 robots per 10,000 manufacturing employees, significantly below the global average of 177.
The Yorkshire Robotics Adoption Hub will help businesses move from initial interest through feasibility, business case development and supplier selection to full deployment. The programme aims to engage more than 300 manufacturers, deliver 80 feasibility studies and support at least 30 robotics deployments.
Professor Ben Whiteside, Principal Investigator, Director of the Institute of Digital and Sustainable Futures at the University of Bradford, said: “Yorkshire has one of the strongest manufacturing bases in the country, yet too many businesses still struggle to move from interest in robotics to successful deployment.
“The challenge isn’t that companies don’t want to automate. The challenge is that many lack the time, expertise or confidence to take the next step.
“This Hub brings together universities, manufacturers, technology providers and business support organisations to bridge that gap. By helping businesses adopt proven technologies, we can improve productivity, strengthen supply chains and support long-term economic growth across the region.

items.title: From Detection to Resolution: The Anatomy of a Supply Chain Exception
items.description: From Detection to Resolution: The Anatomy of a Supply Chain Exception can be understood as a closed operating loop rather than a dashboard workflow. A mature exception capability moves through detection, qualification, context, decision, authority, action, and feedback. The post From Detection to Resolution: The Anatomy of a Supply Chain Exception appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A mature supply-chain exception should be managed as a closed operating loop rather than as a dashboard workflow. The capability must detect a meaningful change, assemble context, assess consequence, determine the appropriate response, execute or escalate within guardrails, and verify whether the intervention worked.
The first stage is observation: an ETA changes, a tender is rejected, inventory becomes unavailable, a facility constraint emerges, or an external risk event alters the plan. Detection should be timely and tied to a persistent business entity rather than delivered as an isolated message. The earlier decision-architecture framework provides the governance spine for this lifecycle: context, authority, escalation, execution, and verification all have to remain connected as the exception moves toward resolution.
The system then needs to qualify the event against service commitments, customer priority, inventory, downstream dependencies, financial exposure, and time to intervene. This is where an alert becomes an exception.
Relevant data may live across several systems. Visibility and execution systems produce events; an intelligence and orchestration layer determines which changes matter; decision rights and workflow determine whether software recommends, prepares, escalates, or executes; TMS, WMS, ERP, OMS, YMS, and partner systems carry out the response The platform should gather enough state to explain why the condition matters, what constraints apply, and which responses are feasible.
The response can be recommended, prepared, auto-executed within a threshold, or escalated. Authority should be explicit. Cost limits, service thresholds, policy rules, data confidence, and customer consequence all help determine how much autonomy is appropriate.
The chosen action must reach the system or partner that can change physical execution. Then the operation should observe whether the action worked. If the intervention fails or creates a new constraint, the loop begins again with updated state.

items.excerpt:
Origin , a full-stack physical AI company building general-purpose robots for interior construction, has emerged from stealth with $20 million in total funding, co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures.
Other backers include Unilazer Ventures, Schema Ventures and Z21, alongside angel investors from Anduril, Skild AI, 1X and Tesla.
The funding will primarily go toward deploying OG-1, Origin’s flagship robot, and building out its fleet. It will also support large-scale pilots with customers in the US and Europe – including two of the largest drywall finishing contractors in the US, with additional pilots scheduled in Germany, Sweden, France and Saudi Arabia – and extend the platform to new interior trades.
From housing and factories to warehouses and AI data centers, demand for new construction is rising faster than the industry can staff it. Around the world, contractors are being asked to deliver more, faster, with too few skilled workers. A 2026 survey found that worker shortages delayed projects for 42 percent of responding US construction firms.
Rising costs, inconsistent quality and stagnant productivity add to the pressure, stretching schedules and limiting the projects contractors can take on. Origin is building robots to help crews increase capacity, deliver consistently and turn that demand into revenue.
Vivin Hegde, founding partner at Zacua Ventures, says: “Too many construction robots perform well in a lab and fail within a week on a live job site. Origin built for the job site from the start, and it shows in the results: the robot works, crews trust it and the company can manufacture it at volume.

items.title: Workforce Readiness is Bottleneck for Supply Chain AI Adoption
items.description: A new study from ASCM found 83% of companies say their workers are unprepared to use AI effectively.
items.excerpt:
The technology might be ready, but the humans don't seem to be. At least that's the conclusion of a study, The People Paradox in Supply Chain AI Integration, released by the Association for Supply Chain Management (ASCM) and the Digital Supply Chain Institute (DSCI) .
The study found that while 91% of organizations plan to use AI to augment human workers, 83% say their employees are unprepared to use AI effectively.
The research finds that the biggest obstacles to scaling AI are not executive skepticism or a lack of buy-in. Instead, organizations face four business hurdles: an unready workforce, an inability to trust AI to act autonomously, cybersecurity concerns, and persistent difficulty proving return on investment.
The result is a high-interest, low-execution cycle in which companies hold AI on a short leash until talent, trust, and measurable business value catch up.
“AI adoption in supply chain is more about people than it is technology,” said ASCM CEO Abe Eshkenazi in a statement. “The organizations making real progress treat workforce readiness as part of the technology investment, not an afterthought. They learn by doing, bring managers into the process early, and build trust one function at a time.”
Workforce readiness is the top bottleneck : 83% of respondents say their employees are unprepared to use AI effectively, and only 14% say their organizations are fully prepared for an AI-augmented future. Just 7% expect AI to directly replace workers, while 51% expect it to shift people toward higher-value decision-making and 40% expect new roles to emerge.
AI is kept on a short leash: Across 13 core supply chain functions, average AI adoption scores just 1.94 on a five-point scale ranging from no use (1) to fully autonomous execution (5). Planning leads, with demand planning at 2.28 and supply and inventory planning at 2.12, while execution-heavy functions trail. Reverse logistics ranks lowest at 1.59.
Strategy is trapped at the top: 82% of C-suite leaders actively lead, implement or scale AI initiatives, but direct leadership drops to 12% at the director level. Half of directors, 51% of managers, and 70% of staff say they are aware of AI initiatives without being actively involved.

Google Developers Blog 发布教程，讲解如何用开源 ADK 与 gemini-3.8-live 构建不出现冷场的语音智能体，核心是非阻塞工具调用。

一份关于 流式工具 、非阻塞函数调用以及 Agent Development Kit (ADK) Gemini Live API Toolkit 中响应调度的指南。
在文本聊天中，一次耗时 13 秒的数据库查询或 RAG 流水线只会显示一个加载转圈。而在实时语音对话中，13 秒的阻塞式工具执行会产生 13 秒的静默，导致用户以为通话已断开而挂断。
你无法总是让后端查询在亚秒级完成，因此修复方案必须从架构层面入手：在慢速工具于后台运行的同时，让代理保持对话。开源 ADK 和 gemini-3.8-live 让你无需自行编写客户端 WebSocket 事件循环来管理异步工具状态，即可用 Python 原生实现非阻塞语音工具。在我们基于 gemini-3.8-live 的基准销售报告工作流中，从阻塞式工具切换为流式工具后，代理说出第一句话的时间从 14.4 秒缩短到了 1.2 秒。
本指南介绍如何使用流式工具、非阻塞 FunctionTool 定义以及 response_scheduling 来构建响应迅速、自然的语音代理。

在标准代理开发中，工具被定义为一个 async def 函数，它完成工作并返回单个值：
当直接传给 ADK 中的 Agent 时，该函数会创建一个阻塞式工具调用。在 Gemini Live API 双向语音会话（ run_live ）中，执行循环会等待工具返回，然后才生成后续的模型轮次。
如果 query_sales_database 耗时 13 秒，代理就会产生 13 秒的完全沉默。诸如“告诉用户你正在处理”之类的提示指令无法解决这个问题，因为模型的轮次被阻塞，正在等待函数响应负载。
为了让对话保持流畅，你可以根据期望的用户体验，在两种主要的非阻塞模式之间进行选择。
当一个操作由多个有意义的阶段组成（例如连接数据库、聚合记录、格式化结果）时， 流式工具 可以让智能体在进度发生时进行叙述。
在 ADK 中，将标准工具转换为流式工具只需把 return 改为 yield 。通过将函数定义为 AsyncGenerator ，ADK 会自动将该工具声明标记为 NON_BLOCKING ，并向模型返回一个即时的状态确认。
持续不断的进度解说并不总是合适的。如果用户要求生成一份报告，然后立即转向另一个话题，那么一个不断用状态更新打断的智能体会让人感到烦扰。
要在没有持续进度絮叨的情况下获得即时的口头确认，一个有效的方法是使用一个仅在完成时产出一次的异步生成器：
由于这是一个异步生成器，ADK 会立即发出一个待处理响应。智能体会迅速确认请求（“我正在为您整理那份报告”），在计算期间保持沉默，并在数据准备好后或用户说完话时呈现这些数据。
如果你希望保留标准协程（ async def ... -> dict ），请将函数包装在 FunctionTool 中并配置 response_scheduling ：
理解权衡： 当使用 response_scheduling 搭配仅返回一次结果的协程时，模型在整个函数完成之前不会收到任何数据。因此，除非用户继续说话，模型通常不会给出最初的口头确认。当用户立即继续提出其他问题，而你希望结果在下一个自然停顿处融入对话时，这种模式最为理想。
response_scheduling 属性控制模型 何时 对传入的工具响应做出反应。 WHEN_IDLE 绝不会打断正在进行的轮次：如果模型仍在说话或用户仍在讲话，结果会等到该轮次结束后再处理，模型会在下一个自然停顿处做出响应。ADK 支持三种调度行为：
执行形态（流式传输与单次返回）和投递时机（ response_scheduling ）相互独立，可以组合使用。在流式工具上设置 response_scheduling 会为每个部分更新打上该行为标记。
此外，在 ADK 2.8 及更新版本中，流式工具可以通过产出 types.FunctionResponse 为每次更新动态指定调度：
经验法则： 如果等待有故事可讲，就流式传输。如果等待只是等待，就在后台运行，让结果在空闲时落地。
非阻塞工具不会减少后端执行时间：一个 13 秒的查询仍然需要 13 秒。改变的是你的智能体在对话中的存在感。
一个需要十秒才能加载的 Web 应用会被认为很慢；一个沉默十秒的对话式语音智能体则会被认为出了故障。通过将 ADK 的流式工具和灵活的响应调度与 gemini-3.8-live 的实时能力相结合，你可以构建在复杂操作全程中保持专注、自然且在场的语音助手。
亲自尝试： 交互式演示 在 gemini-3.8-live 上通过每种工具模式和 response_scheduling 模式运行同一个 13 秒查询，让你能听出差异。

items.title: Scope 3 Is Not Primarily a Reporting Problem. It Is a Supply Chain Data Problem
items.description: Scope 3 is fundamentally a supply-chain data architecture problem. Credibility depends on boundaries, activity data, factor governance, allocation, lineage, and explicit uncertainty—not on a more polished reporting layer. The post Scope 3 Is Not Primarily a Reporting Problem. It Is a Supply Chain Data Problem appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Executive thesis. Scope 3 is fundamentally a supply-chain data architecture problem. Credibility depends on boundaries, activity data, factor governance, allocation, lineage, and explicit uncertainty—not on a more polished reporting layer.
Scope 3 reporting is often described as a carbon-accounting challenge, but much of the difficulty is more fundamental: obtaining reliable activity data across suppliers, carriers, products, facilities, and other parts of the value chain. When primary data is incomplete, organizations rely on estimates, factors, and allocation methods that introduce uncertainty. The quality of the result therefore depends on the quality and lineage of the underlying supply chain data.
Before calculation begins, the organization needs clear boundaries for which activities, entities, shipments, products, and periods are included. Inconsistent boundaries can create apparent changes that are methodological rather than operational. Governance should make those choices explicit and preserve them so results can be reproduced and compared over time.
Spend-based estimates can provide coverage when better information is unavailable, but operational activity data generally creates more effective insight. Shipment distance, mode, weight, equipment, fuel, energy, supplier activity, and other physical measures can connect emissions more directly to the processes the enterprise can change. That is what turns Scope 3 from a reporting exercise into a management tool.
A precise number can create false confidence if the source data is weak. Mature programs expose data quality, estimation methods, factor versions, allocation logic, and uncertainty. That allows leaders to distinguish categories where measurement is already decision-grade from areas where improving primary-data coverage should be the immediate priority.
The objective is not only to improve the inventory. It is to identify where operational changes can reduce emissions: mode shifts, utilization, routing, carrier choices, supplier changes, energy improvements, packaging, product design, or network configuration. Better data is valuable because it makes those levers easier to quantify and prioritize.

items.title: 德国两家法院先后裁定 Google 须为其 AI Overview 内容负责
items.description: 慕尼黑地区法院 I 五月底裁定 Google 的 AI 搜索摘要属于公司自己的陈述而非中立转述，Google 须为错误内容担责；Google 公开宣布上诉后实际以和解结案，未获上级法院裁决。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/bbr25r9mbi8zbbtmu2uiati7f
items.excerpt:
Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say
慕尼黑地区法院 I 五月底裁定 Google 的 AI 搜索摘要属于公司自己的陈述而非中立转述，Google 须为错误内容担责；Google 公开宣布上诉后实际以和解结案，未获上级法院裁决。
两起德国法院判例指向同一法律逻辑，文章还分析了 Google 以和解回避判例对 AI 搜索商业模式的潜在影响。
Google曾试图通过上诉推翻慕尼黑一项关于AI搜索摘要责任的里程碑式裁决，随后悄然达成和解。如今，第二家法院采用了同样的推理。Google的AI回答被视为该公司自身的内容，Google需对其负责。
5月下旬，慕尼黑地区法院第一庭在一桩 备受关注的案件 中裁定，Google对其AI生成的搜索摘要内容负有直接责任。Google的AI曾错误地将两家慕尼黑出版商与欺诈计划关联。法官将AI概览归类为Google自身的陈述，而非单纯的搜索结果，这意味着该公司本身必须为其负责。
Google无法再躲在传递第三方信息的中立中间人角色背后，而必须为其AI生成的不法陈述承担责任。对于一个不断生成新答案的搜索功能而言，这是一种难以量化的法律风险。如果这一观点成立，可能会动摇德国AI搜索的整个商业模式，并影响其他国家的相关讨论。
搜索引用与原创内容之间的区分还可能产生超出虚假事实陈述之外的后果。如果AI回答被视为Google自身的内容，那么Google用来生成这些回答的文本所属的出版商，最终可能会主张自己的权利。这并非慕尼黑案件的一部分，但却是合乎逻辑的下一步。
据THE DECODER了解， Google公开宣布的上诉 从未走到裁决阶段。案件最终以和解告终，这意味着没有任何上级法院对慕尼黑的推理作出评判。为何达成和解以及是否涉及金钱往来尚不清楚。Google和受影响的出版商均拒绝置评。法院也拒绝就其裁决在具体案件之外的更广泛意义发表意见。
不过，慕尼黑法官的法律推理并未消亡。在 2026年9月24日的一项裁决中，亚琛地区法院 禁止Google传播某些虚假陈述，并明确援引了慕尼黑裁决的推理。Google可以对该禁令提出异议。该裁决尚未最终生效。
在这起新案件中，亚琛的一位医生对Google“AI模式”搜索功能中的严重虚假指控进行了反击。这位医生自2010年起至2026年6月下旬担任神经放射学首席医师和教授。8月28日，一位同事提醒他，Google的AI在解释其离职时，援引了一起据称针对其秘书的性侵事件。当用户使用“停职”“解雇”和“法庭程序”等词进行进一步搜索时，AI模式返回了详细的多段捏造内容。它甚至编造了完整的法律后续。
这些指控和程序均与该医生毫无关系。AI将涉及另一位前大学教授的事件安在了他身上，亚琛法院可以从自己的记录中确认这一点，因为刑事案件实际上是对另一个人提起的。 此类AI错误归因的案例 此前已有 记录 。
尽管医生在8月底详细描述了这一混淆情况，并通过电子邮件要求谷歌删除相关内容，但该公司在9月中旬表示不会采取任何行动。同日发出的正式法律要求同样没有下文。谷歌确认已收到该要求，但据法院称，这些由AI生成的虚假文本当时仍在线。
随后，亚琛地区法院禁止进一步传播三个有争议的文本版本。由于这些虚假陈述可能严重损害医生的职业声誉，法院在未听取谷歌意见的情况下采取了紧急行动。如果谷歌违反该命令，每次违规将面临最高25万欧元的罚款。
亚琛裁决最重要的部分在于它与慕尼黑推理的高度一致，这表明德国法院正在形成一致的法律观点。谷歌利用其AI生成自己的陈述，而非仅仅让第三方信息可被找到。法院写道：“被申请人提供AI生成的搜索，因此也应对在此背景下生成的答案负责。”
亚琛甚至直接引用了慕尼黑的裁决，指出谷歌的AI基于对多个第三方网站内容的评估和组合，生成“独立的、新的、实质性的陈述”。
法院表示，谷歌可以核查此类陈述，例如将其AI输出与其使用的来源网站进行比对。亚琛的法官还补充说，如果谷歌让其自家AI面对医生的异议，系统本会自行发现这些错误。
两起案件都引发了人们对谷歌针对其AI搜索功能所采取长期法律策略的疑问。如果德国法院继续将该公司归类为虚假陈述的发布者，而谷歌继续通过很可能是财务和解的方式规避判例，就会形成一种反常的激励。
对于专业律师事务所和受影响方而言，这可能变成一种有利可图的商业模式。他们可以用有针对性的查询探测AI搜索，直到语言模型拼凑出虚假、可能具有诽谤性的陈述，然后申请禁令并协商和解。这些系统很容易被操纵。
当然，谷歌有能力以这种方式让个别案件消失多年，因为只有至少一方将法律程序推进到底，才会形成具有约束力的判例。但谷歌的动机很可能远不止对个别虚假陈述的责任。如果最高法院裁定AI答案算作原创内容，那么为这些答案提供文本的发布者也可以主张自己的权利。在最极端的情况下，谷歌将不得不就其来源背后的创作者为每个AI生成的答案进行补偿。这将彻底颠覆AI搜索的经济模式。

items.description: 作者分享受邀参加英伟达 RTX Spark 全球开售活动后，深度使用一周华硕 ProArt 创16（128G 统一内存+1T，京东售价 37999 元）的体验，开售时 128G 版本在京东几分钟内被抢空。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/i8vi0763u7lz34lkoagoh0agt
items.excerpt:
作者分享受邀参加英伟达 RTX Spark 全球开售活动后，深度使用一周华硕 ProArt 创16（128G 统一内存+1T，京东售价 37999 元）的体验，开售时 128G 版本在京东几分钟内被抢空。
作者亲测 RTX Spark 上的本地模型部署路径，并把整套流程封装成 WorkBuddy 专家，读者可以照着复现本地 Token 自由的用法。
https://x.com/i/article/2111639179931291648
昨天，受邀在北京参加英伟达的活动，跟他们一起在店里庆祝，RTX Spark的全球开售。
在剪彩开售的一瞬间，我去京东看了下，几分钟不到，128G的版本，直接就被抢空了？？？
而我自己呢，其实在一周以前就已经收到了RTX Spark的机器，是华硕的ProArt创16，128G统一内存+1T版本，目前在京东售价37999，也就是上面那个在京东直接被抢空的版本。在所有的同机型里，性价比应该是最高的了，其他的同型号有的甚至要贵上万块。
你很难想象，这么一台薄至约12.9mm、轻至1.79kg的16英寸轻薄本，里面居然塞进了一颗原生支持CUDA、最高拥有128GB统一内存的RTX Spark芯片。
目前我也已经深度使用了一周的时间了，非常想跟大家来分享一下我在这段时间，使用RTX Spark的体验。
其实今年6月，老黄第一次在发布会上发布RTX Spark 的时候，我就写过一篇文章：英伟达发布全新RTX Spark - 个人PC的新时代。
在那之后，我其实就一直等着这台电脑发售，虽然我现在有两台Mac Mini在家24小时跑着Agent，但是谁又能拒绝一个有着统一内存，还有CUDA生态，能在本地跑模型，还能打游戏的超轻薄的RTX Spark电脑呢。
你想要大内存，那可能就得买 Mac。苹果的统一内存确实很牛逼，但是很多AI项目的底层都是围绕NVIDIA的CUDA生态开发的，在Mac上跑起来，有时候就需要各种移植和适配。
你想用CUDA呢，那就得买英伟达显卡。但是传统消费级显卡的显存容量又有限，5090也才32G，稍微大一点的模型，就有可能塞不进去。
128GB的统一内存，加上CUDA生态，作为一个喜欢折腾AI、并且还是一个游戏佬的我来说，没办法，RTX Spark还是太有吸引力了，而且基本就是唯一解。
所以一周以前拿到手以后，我除了先下了Steam之外，干的第一件事，就是开始疯狂去部署各种各样的模型。
我知道，大家肯定都还会想跟5090比一下，但这块我想说，RTX Spark主打的还是大容量、便携、以及超高能效。
为了大容量和轻量便携，所以英伟达做了一些妥协，压低了带宽和算力，但是换来的，是完全不同功耗。
RTX Spark把功耗压到了80W，而5090纯单显卡，就需要恐怖的575w的功耗，你在笔记本和一些小机型里，根本不可能带的动。
所以，相比之下，我个人还是觉得，对于绝大多数的玩家来说，RTX Spark的适用性和泛化性，还是高于5090的，基本就是用更加广泛的场景，来换取慢一点的速度。
因为这一次英伟达为了让大家开箱即用，所以也贴心的跟WorkBuddy合作了，他们搞了一个RTX Spark专区，所以国内用户完全可以直接下载WorkBuddy，这样可以非常方便的开箱即用。
首先，打开WorkBuddy，在左上角找到这个RTX Spark专区，然后点击切换。
当然，最核心的，肯定还是在这台电脑上，使用本地模型，我都用RTX Spark了，那肯定是要用本地模型的嘛对吧。
如果你是第一次拿到这台设备，那右边是一个下载的选项，就可以直接一键把模型下载下来放到你的本地了。
同样的，你也可以自己部署其他的模型，不需知道太底层的原理，可以直接让Agent帮你跑。
对于一台128G统一内存的机器来说，吃下一个100B左右的Q4量化版本，我觉得是没啥问题的，但是相对于日常使用来说，我不建议跑的这么满，需要给别的东西留下一点空间。
所以，我无比推荐大家，换上我觉得本地的一个最牛逼的模型，甚至是能跟曾经的Opus 4.6相匹敌的，且能无时无刻常驻后台的模型。
这玩意是真的猛，猛到一定的级别了，在AA上，以一个27B的模型，跟一众几千亿的模型打的有来有回。
想在本地部署它，并且在WorkBuddy里一起用，或者放到别的Agent里面变成可选模型，也特别简单。
这里要注意，即使开了MTP后，Qwen3.8-27B的推理速度，还是会比比如Qwen3.6-35B-A3B慢不少，主要是因为这是一个少见的Dense模型，所以其实推理的时候也是带着27B的参数一起推理的，而后者其实只需要跑3B，所以会慢不少。
我在本地实测大概能跑到30 Token/秒，差不多跟Codex里面的GPT-6.1 Sol一个速度，所以你能接受GPT-6.1 Sol的速度，那我觉得在本地跑Qwen-3.8 27B，我觉得你也没啥问题。
部署到本地以后，你就可以让他快乐的干活了，至此，你也拥有了，无限Token，想怎么干活怎么干活。

Meta took the lead of this charge with Muse Spark Open , which is now the strongest American-made open model by quite some margin, but the addition of Reflection’s first model Beam is also relevant. items.description: Sustainability technology is moving from disclosure infrastructure toward operational decision support. The post Supply Chain Sustainability Software Is Moving From Disclosure to Operational Decision-Making appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Executive thesis. Sustainability technology is moving from disclosure infrastructure toward operational decision support. Carbon and ESG data become strategically relevant only when they change sourcing, transportation, facility, product, or supplier decisions.
Supply chain sustainability technology developed largely around measurement and disclosure: calculate emissions, collect supplier information, produce reports, and demonstrate compliance. Those functions remain necessary, but they do not by themselves reduce impact. The strategic value appears when sustainability data begins to influence sourcing, network, transportation, facility, product, and supplier decisions.
Carbon accounting, supplier ESG, product footprints, transportation emissions, traceability, and reduction planning are related but not identical capabilities. They rely on different activity data, factors, boundaries, evidence, and operating workflows. Buyers should therefore start with the decisions the business needs to support rather than assume one sustainability platform can solve every problem equally well.
A defensible metric needs more than a calculated result. The enterprise should be able to trace boundaries, source data, factor versions, allocation rules, transformations, and overrides. This is especially material as sustainability information influences external reporting, customer commitments, procurement decisions, and capital allocation.
Sustainability systems become more consequential when they connect to procurement, ERP, TMS, facilities, products, carriers, and suppliers. Those connections allow the enterprise to compare operational alternatives before execution rather than calculate the environmental effect after the fact. The data architecture is therefore part of the sustainability strategy.
The effective question is not how many dashboards the organization can produce. It is whether the platform helps identify and prioritize reduction levers with an understandable economic and operational impact. Better mode selection, improved utilization, supplier changes, energy decisions, product redesign, and network changes are examples of actions that turn sustainability information into operating value.

US Open-Weights Push: Muse Spark Open and Reflection Beam
Muse Spark Open (Meta) : An 816B-total, 42B-active MoE with open weights. Artificial Analysis scores it 39 on its Intelligence Index, the highest for a US open-weights model and 13 points above NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 Super VL at 26 ( AA ).
Architecture and footprint : 62 layers, GQA with 16 KV heads, 8 of 256 experts active per token, a 1.8B Perception Encoder and 1M context. Inputs are text, image, video and audio; output is text. BF16 weights are about 1.6TB. Meta’s NVFP4 checkpoint quantizes only the experts, cutting weights to about 530GB. Meta says that fits on 4 Blackwell Ultra GPUs, 8 H200s or two 512GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios.
Pricing and efficiency : Together, Fireworks and Baseten charge $1.25/$4.25 per M input/output tokens, with $0.15 cached input. AA puts the cost at $0.84 per index task, versus $2.01 for GLM-5.3 and $0.27 for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. It uses 40k output tokens per task, the fewest among the top nine open models ( cost ). Vals counts 55.5M output tokens across its index, the fewest of any open model, but says input tokens drive most of its cost ( Vals ).
Weak spot : It ranks last among the top nine open models on AA’s four agentic evals while leading open models on AA-Omniscience. Vals places it #12 among open-weight models and #38 overall ( Vals ). Arena ranks it the top US open model on Code Arena WebDev with 1511 points, #13 among open models ( Arena ).
License : The custom Muse Model License requires “Built with Muse Spark Open” attribution. Model-as-a-Service businesses with more than $20M in annual revenue need a separate agreement with Meta.

items.title: Anthropic 如何在 Claude 写下 Claude Code 约 90% 代码后重新设计代码评审
items.description: 作者解读 Anthropic 关于 Claude Code 代码评审重构的博客：Claude 写了约 90% 的代码，2026 年 6 月到 9 月合并 PR 翻倍以上而 revert 率下降超 40%。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/p4mq9t7wyzlxritu15i6d8dtv
items.excerpt:
作者解读 Anthropic 关于 Claude Code 代码评审重构的博客：Claude 写了约 90% 的代码，2026 年 6 月到 9 月合并 PR 翻倍以上而 revert 率下降超 40%。
原文拆解了 Anthropic 重构代码评审的七层防线和收敛问题的具体解法，对引入 AI reviewer 的团队有可迁移的做法。
当 Claude 写了 Claude Code 约 90% 的代码后，团队如何重新设计代码评审 ？
Anthropic 没有取消代码评审，是把 “人读代码” 这个动作大部分交给了机器，把稀缺的人类注意力只花在真正需要判断力的地方。核心转变是：从“这段代码有人看过吗”变成“这个变更可能出什么问题，哪种检查（自动或人工）最适合抓住它”。 https://claude.dev/blog/solving-code-review-at-anthropic/
背景数字：2026 年 6 月到 9 月，合并的 PR 数量翻倍以上，而 revert 率下降超 40%。传统的“同事互相读 diff”模式在这个吞吐量下会先崩溃；人要么变成瓶颈，要么敷衍放行。
团队对成本的认识很清醒：人力时间 = 评审时间 + 修复坏代码的时间，压缩一头只会把成本转移到另一头。所以他们不追踪“评审覆盖率”这种虚荣指标，而转去追踪 “每个 PR 平均几个人类审批” 和 “等人审批的等待时间”，并以 revert 率 / 事故率作为护栏指标；目标是最多一个人在环（有时只有作者本人），且事故不比以前多。
1. PR 之前的自我验证 — Claude 必须出示证据（测试输出、构建、截图）而不是声称完成；再用一个全新上下文的第二个 agent 审 diff。Boris Cherny（Claude Code 创造者）认为给 Claude 一个验证方法是“最重要的事”，效果提升 2–3 倍。反复出现的问题会被固化到源头：写进 CLAUDE.md（项目约定）和 REVIEW.md（给代码主人看的指引——失败长什么样、nit 上限、哪些路径跳过，且每条发现必须附文件/行号证据）。
2. 每个 PR 必过 AI 评审 — 内部 PR 上“实质性评审意见”占比从 16% 升到 54%；千行以上的大 PR 几乎总能查出问题。多个 agent 并行找 bug，再有 verifier agent 对每条发现投票才发出。发现分为 Important / Nit / Pre-existing，每条必须解决或说明理由。
4. 阻塞性的自动检查 — lint、类型、跨平台测试、构建；PR 模板强制填写“如何测试的”和“如何回滚”，且需一人签字。
5. 基于风险的人工审批 — 分类器定级：低风险（文档、文案）不需人工；中风险（普通产品变更，及缓存、自动更新器、系统提示词等敏感区）一人；高风险两人。关键规则：agent 的批准永远不能算人工批准；批准只覆盖一个 commit，有新提交就要重新审批。
6. 合并队列 + 特性开关 + 灰度 — 针对合并后 main 重跑检查；新行为先给 Anthropic 内部员工，再走 latest channel，最后进 stable。
7. 快速检测与回滚 — 开关无需重新部署即可关闭；事故复盘必问“哪一层本该拦住它”。
1. 评审器本身也是被持续评测的系统。 过去引发事故的 PR（经专家确认）构成一个 eval 集，评审器每天跑分，只有分数提升的改动才被保留；噪声则通过“人对评论的反应”和“在已知干净的 PR 上跑评审器”来度量。这本质上是把“评审质量”从主观感受变成了可优化的目标函数。
2. 收敛问题的解法。 曾有一个 agent 写的 CLI PR 一夜跑了 50+ 轮评审，而 git blame 显示约 59% 被标记的代码在第一轮之前就存在；评审 agent 在翻旧账而不是审新变更。修复手段：三轮封顶（超过就退回来重新考虑方案）、后续轮次只看增量 diff、标记 bug 类别而非单行、禁止重复发现。效果：一轮通过率 65%→78%，5 轮以上 PR 从 8.9% 降到 1.5%，平均评审轮次 2.08→1.32。这是 AI 评审 AI 代码时特有的“死循环”问题，他们的解法值得所有引入 AI reviewer 的团队抄作业。
· 该不该做：方向、品味、范围； · 高危代码：计费、自动更新器、CI 工作流； · 可被复制模仿的架构决策； · 读证据：测试输出、截图、发现列表； · 为结果负责：每个上线变更背后必须有一个承担问责的人。
原文拆解了 Anthropic 重构代码评审的七层防线和收敛问题的具体解法，对引入 AI reviewer 的团队有可迁移的做法。

Integrated Systems Design, or ISD, last week launched its Palletizing Module, which builds outbound pallets and breaks down incoming ones in a single cell. Most competing systems handle only one direction, requiring separate equipment, separate floor space, and separate capital budgets for each function, according to the company.

ISD’s Palletizing Module includes a robotic arm, custom end-of-arm tooling, machine vision, and integrated controls. The vision system identifies box or case dimensions in real time and adjusts placement patterns accordingly, whether the robot is building a pallet or breaking one down. items.excerpt:
Great digital products rarely arrive fully formed. For startups, product teams, and established companies testing a new concept, custom MVP app development services can turn a promising idea into a working product before time, budget, and internal energy are spent in the wrong direction.
An MVP is not a rough draft thrown into the market. It is a focused version of a product built to test real demand, collect user feedback, and prove whether the concept has commercial potential. Instead of building everything at once, companies start with the core function that solves a specific problem. Then they learn. Then they improve.
This approach is especially valuable in markets where customer expectations change quickly. A product that looked perfect during internal planning can feel irrelevant once users interact with it. MVP development helps avoid that trap. It gives businesses a faster, safer, and more practical way to move from assumption to evidence.
A successful MVP is not defined by how many features it has. It is defined by how clearly it tests the main product hypothesis. The best MVPs are simple, sharp, and useful.
Every MVP should begin with a specific problem. Vague ideas usually lead to vague products. The team must understand who the users are, what they struggle with, and why the proposed solution is better than existing alternatives.
For example, “a productivity app” is too broad. “An app that helps field service teams report completed jobs with photos and digital signatures” is clearer. The second idea gives the development team something concrete to build and test.
An MVP should include only the features needed to deliver the core value. Everything else can wait. This discipline is difficult because teams often want to add more. More filters. More dashboards. More user roles. More integrations.
But every extra feature increases complexity, cost, and testing effort. A focused MVP protects the project from becoming too heavy too early.
Minimal does not mean unpleasant. Users still expect clear navigation, understandable screens, and a smooth basic experience. If the MVP is confusing, feedback may reflect poor usability rather than the strength of the idea.
Good UX design helps users understand the product quickly. It also makes early feedback more reliable.

D-Wave Quantum Inc. , a provider of quantum computing systems, software, and services, and the University of Arkansas are launching an initiative to explore the role quantum computing could play in supply chain management.
The initiative, which was announced at the Council of Supply Chain Management Professionals’ EDGE Conference on Monday, will be part of the Supply Chain Management Research Center (SMRC) at the Sam M. Walton College of Business .
Quantum computing is an emerging area of computing that researchers are exploring for certain complex optimization problems, including routing, scheduling, and resource allocation.
“Supply chains are highly dynamic, with decision-making that can have a far-reaching impact on efficiency and costs,” said Murray Thom, vice president of quantum technology evangelism at D-Wave. “We’re seeing quantum computing technologies emerge as potentially powerful alternatives to existing classical approaches.”
The collaboration between D-Wave and the SCMRC will explore foundational and applied research in quantum optimization for supply chain use cases, including transportation routing, logistics network design, inventory and resource allocation, scheduling, and decision-making under disruption. The organizations also may collaborate on curriculum development, case studies, practical frameworks and student-learning opportunities.
“The Walton College is dedicated to exploring the very latest methods, processes and technologies that advance supply chain management and resilience,” said Brian Fugate, Associate Dean for Research and Graduate Programs with Walton College. “Quantum computing is showing great potential to help organizations accelerate decision-making, mitigate disruption and drive better operational outcomes.” We’re excited to partner with D-Wave, one of the quantum computing industry’s foremost leaders, to bring quantum into our research portfolio and ultimately benefit students and partners alike.”

items.excerpt:
First Global Sustainable Logistics Survey sets baseline for UN Decade of Sustainable Transport initiative, examines key aspects of sustainability across logistics and supply chain.
Logistics service providers, manufacturers, and retailers largely agree on the measures that cut emissions and promote sustainability in logistics, but they struggle to scale them, according to results of the first Global Sustainable Logistics Survey (GSLS), released this week by Kühne Logistics University (KLU) and the Kuehne Climate Center (KCC).
The survey polled 1,085 professionals from 64 countries about sustainable logistics, covering three topics: sustainability solutions, skills, and adaptation to climate risks.
“Across all three areas, the same pattern emerges: professionals broadly agree on what needs to happen, but progress depends on whether individual companies, or the wider systems they rely on, are actually able to act,” GSLS researchers wrote in the inaugural report, which they say is the first global, longitudinal study on sustainable logistics and sets a baseline for tracking the sector over the United Nations (UN) Decade of Sustainable Transport initiative .
The report also makes recommendations for policymakers and logistics professionals on scaling sustainability solutions, building skills, and adapting to climate risks.
For policymakers, those recommendations include developing a “context-specific enabling policy framework” for sustainable logistics: “Frameworks should focus on solutions that are rated effective but rarely adopted, such as low-carbon fuels, electrification, and intermodal transport,” according to the report.
For managers, recommendations include moving ahead with capital-intensive solutions while demanding changes in policy frameworks: “Companies that move early build know-how and meet customer expectations before regulation requires it. Investments can be staged while preserving flexibility,” according to the report.
The survey and full report are available online from the Kuehne Climate Center.
